summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 34.3 minutes, and 4 were compute-bound. Local scored-stack ARC selfparse dry run was the longest listed task at 24.76 minutes. The evidence records no compute-bound GPU-idle fault, but it does not provide a causal phase breakdown or parallel-model dispatch data.
bottlenecks_identified: Local scored-stack ARC selfparse dry run was the longest listed task at 24.76 minutes; no data available this milestone explains which phase caused that duration.
Execution-aligned phase, GPU, model-count, and runner-choice telemetry was unavailable, so compute efficiency and parallel-dispatch eligibility could not be audited.
improvements_suggested: Add task-scoped phase timers and periodic GPU samples from compute-bound task start through completion.
Add checkpoint and reusable preparation caches to the scored-stack ARC path, then measure each phase before setting a runtime gate.
Emit model-count, runner-choice, and DualGPURunner-eligibility receipts before compute launch; select DualGPURunner only when at least two models load in parallel.
Schedule independent synthesis-only work concurrently with the compute-bound critical path when task dependencies allow.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument the scored-stack ARC path with phase timers and compute-window GPU telemetry.
Checkpoint the scored-stack ARC path and cache unchanged model and input preparation work.
Record model concurrency and runner selection at launch, with DualGPURunner reserved for parallel multi-model tasks.
meta_reflection: The timing data is sufficient to rank the critical path but not to diagnose its cause. The reported GPU snapshot and absent concurrency receipt do not support a compute-window efficiency verdict, a missed DualGPURunner claim, or a measured savings estimate.
